div.head: II Atr 9.2
div.ab: Gyf hwa to deadan tyme — buton he yrfenoman hæbbe, ðe hit clænsie —, geswutelie mid gewitnysse, gif he mæge, þæt he riht cenne, se ðe hit tyme; ⁊ clænsnige hine sylfne mid ðam. Ðonne bið se deada besmiten, buton he frind hæbbe, ðe hine mid rihte clænsnian, swa he sylf scolde, gif he mehte oðð lives wære.

Si mortuum hominem aduocet – si non habeat heredes, qui purget eum – manifestet hoc cum testibus, si possit, quod recte aduocet; ac per id se purget. Tunc erit mortuus in culpa, nisi amicos habeat, qui eum mundificent, sicut idem faceret, si posset ac uiueret.

Gyf hwa to deadan tyme—buton he yruenoman hæbbe ðe hit clænsie—geswutelie mid gewitnysse, gyf he mæge, þæt he riht cenne se ðe hit tyme ⁊ clænsnige hine sylfne mid ðam. Ðonne bið se deada besmiten, buton he frind hæbbe ðe hine mid rihte clænsnian, swa he sylf scolde, gif he mehte oðð liues wære.

If anyone vouches a dead person to warranty—unless he have an heir who can answer the charge—he who vouches him to warranty shall show by means of witnesses, if he can, that he is acting justly, and by means of them shall clear himself. Then the dead man will be held guilty, unless he have friends who will clear him according to the law, as he himself would have been obliged to do, had he been able or had he been alive.

Wenn jemand die Gewähr auf einen Verstorbenen zieht — ausser wenn dieser einen Erbnehmer hat, der das [im Anefang Gefasste von Schuld] rein erweisen will —, beweise er, wer es schiebt, durch Zeugenschaft, wenn er kann, dass er richtig [Gewähr] angiebt, und reinige hiermit sich selbst. Dann ist jener Verstorbene [schuld]befleckt, es sei denn, er hat Freunde, die ihn gesetzmässig als rein erweisen, so wie er selbst, wenn er könnte oder am Leben wäre, [es thun] müsste.

If anyone vouches a dead man to warranty — unless he has an heir who will clear [the attached item of guilt] —, let him who vouches it prove by witness, if he can, that he is declaring [the warranty] correctly, and so clear himself. Then the dead man is tainted [with guilt], unless he has friends who will clear him lawfully, as he himself would have had to, if he could or were alive.
